_note: Managers whose 13F book is predominantly index funds and ETFs.
This is an editorial classification, not filed data. A 13F says what a
manager holds, never why: an index fund's shares and a stock-picker's
shares arrive in the same table under the same name. BlackRock files one
13F covering iShares and its active mandates together, and there is no
So the list is deliberately conservative. A name belongs here only if its
13F book is overwhelmingly passive vehicles. Houses that run large active
and passive books side by side -- FMR, JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, Goldman,
Wellington, Capital Research, T. Rowe -- are left out and counted as
active, which understates the index share rather than overstating it.
Matching is case-insensitive on the start of FILINGMANAGER_NAME as the
filer writes it, so one entry catches a manager's several filing
entities (Vanguard files under at least four).
